scope: Actual signed-in React/HTTP/database flow on owned standalone PostgreSQL 18.4 for Windows. Spotify network simulated; no production writes.

checks: 251-track playlist saves through signed-in React UI, actual HTTP routes and database
Canceled replacement sends no POST and preserves both saved sources
Rate limit displays retry guidance and leaves saved playlist and source version unchanged
Later-page failure and changed provider snapshot cannot partially replace saved tracks
Oversized playlist is explicitly rejected, never silently truncated
Confirmed replacement changes only the selected source and advances its version
Two simultaneous replacements with one observed version yield one success and one conflict
A real stale browser preflight cannot overwrite a newer saved playlist
Foreign performer and copied source receipts cannot cross account boundaries
Ownership changed during provider loading is rejected inside the write transaction
Revocation advances source version even with clock skew and rejects a stale restore
Saved source state and account isolation survive process restart
Desktop and mobile Sources journeys have no page errors or horizontal overflow
